title: Your own literals
description:
`10s` and `"text"s` are literals with a suffix the standard library defined. You can define your own. A suffix of your own must start with an underscore.

A literal operator for whole numbers takes `unsigned long long`; one for decimals takes `long double`.

Write:

- `struct Distance { double metres; };`
- `_m` and `_km` literals that work for both whole numbers and decimals (`250_m`, `1.5_km`), giving a `Distance`.
- `operator+` for two distances.
- `_kb` and `_mb` literals for whole numbers, giving a `std::uint64_t` count of bytes (1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB).

Make everything `constexpr`, so `1.5_km + 250_m` is worked out by the compiler.
lessonTitle: Preprocessor Deep Dive, Attributes and User-Defined Literals
